fixture_ref: pr-521::verifier::correctness::fresh::packages/sheets/src/formula/formula.ts::rebuilding the formula string from `extracttokens` output can corrupt formulas whose token text is not verbatim source (whitespace runs, quoted string literals)

decision.reason: I could not verify or refute this finding because the working directory appears empty or inaccessible to my tools. Grep for `expandUnboundedRanges`, `extractTokens`, `token.text`, and `Formula` all returned no matches; Glob for `packages/sheets/src/formula/*.ts`, `**/formula.ts`, `**/*.json`, `packages/**`, and bare `*` all returned no files; and a catch-all Grep for `.` across the tree also returned no files. A catch-all pattern matching zero files indicates a tooling/checkout problem rather than evidence that the described code is absent, so I cannot claim `not-present` — that ground requires positive evidence the code differs from the description, grounded in lines I actually read, and I read none. Treating my own inability to see the tree as a fact about the code would drop a finding from the merge gate on the basis of an infrastructure failure. The finding is independently plausible: reconstructing a formula by concatenating lexer token text is fragile exactly when the grammar `-> skip`s whitespace, because skipped tokens leave gaps concatenation cannot restore, and quoted STRING literals may lose their quotes; the impact would be silent rewriting of a user's stored formula, which is in-lane for Correctness at major severity. Both `packages/sheets/src/formula/formula.ts` and `packages/sheets/antlr/Formula.g4` are on the authoritative changed-file list, so `pre-existing` does not apply either. Per the rule that uncertainty for any reason keeps the finding, I confirm, with low confidence reflecting that I verified the procedure rather than the bug. A re-run on a working checkout should check whether `expandUnboundedRanges` returns `'=' + body`, whether it iterates a hidden-channel-preserving token stream, and whether STRING token text retains quotes.
